title: Simplify Everything
equation: Marketplace Value = Supplier Desire × Partner Desire × Customer Desire
hook: You're guessing what your customers want. So are most founders. You could just ask.
statement: A business gets easier to scale once it clearly knows what each key group of people actually wants.
explainer: Suppliers, partners, and customers all show up for different reasons. Stop guessing on their behalf. Ask each group directly, then build around where their wants overlap.
sop: Pick the stakeholder group you're focused on right now.
Ask them straight up what they want.
Split their answers into nice-to-haves and must-haves.
Score Supplier Desire, Partner Desire, and Customer Desire from 1 to 10.
Build your offer around where those needs overlap.
equation_example: Supplier Desire 7, Partner Desire 6, Customer Desire 8. 7 × 6 × 8 = 336 Marketplace Value. Higher means everyone has a strong reason to stay. If one group's desire drops toward zero, the whole thing collapses, even if the other two are strong.
question: Write down one supplier, partner, or customer you'll ask directly what they want this week.
closing_statement: Your guess about what they want is still a guess.
caption:
Principle Nº 241: Simplify Everything

You're guessing what your customers want. So are most founders. You could just ask.

A business gets easier to scale once it clearly knows what each key group of people actually wants.

Your turn: Write down one supplier, partner, or customer you'll ask directly what they want this week.
